# Sciencx

> > A web development blog exploring JavaScript patterns, web accessibility, UI components, and deployment workflows.

Sciencx features technical articles by Zach Leatherman and others covering progressive enhancement, conservative design principles, browser compatibility, and modern web development practices. The site documents real-world solutions for dynamic UI components, accessibility challenges, and deployment automation.

## Key Topics

- JavaScript patterns and techniques
- Web accessibility and screen readers
- Conservative design principles
- Dynamic UI components (hierarchical selects, form elements)
- Browser event handling and compatibility
- Deployment automation via GitHub
- Progressive enhancement
- JSON and XMLHTTPRequest
- Assistive technology
- Opera browser compatibility
- Umbraco CMS
- HTML and web standards
- UI design patterns
- Victor Tsaran (accessibility expert)
- Flash and web components

## Web Accessibility

- [Screen Readers and Listening at the Speed of Sound](https://www.scien.cx/2007/05/17/screen-readers-and-listening-at-the-speed-of-sound): Web accessibility insights on screen readers featuring Victor Tsaran

## JavaScript & UI Patterns

- [Conservative Design: Hierarchical Select](https://www.scien.cx/2007/02/22/conservative-design-hierarchical-select): Dynamic hierarchical select boxes using JSON/XML with conservative design
- [Don't Let the Door Hit You Onunload and Onbeforeunload](https://www.scien.cx/2008/04/22/don8217t-let-the-door-hit-you-onunload-and-onbeforeunload): Browser event handling for onunload/onbeforeunload with Opera compatibility

## Deployment & DevOps

- [How to deploy sites via GitHub](https://www.scien.cx/2011/11/02/how-to-deploy-sites-via-github): Tutorial on deploying sites via GitHub using SSH and private repos

## Optional

- [Umbraco 4 broke my project!](https://www.scien.cx/2009/02/05/umbraco-4-broke-my-project): Troubleshooting Umbraco 4 upgrade issues and .NET assembly errors
